summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and constipation following recent discharge for secretin-induced pancreatitis. Initial concern for recurrent pancreatitis was tempered by only mildly elevated lipase and a soft, non-tender abdomen. Imaging revealed significant stool burden, and symptoms improved markedly after bowel regimen with polyethylene glycol and senna. Pain resolved, oral intake was advanced successfully, and labs stabilized. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with a soft diet, reduced pancreatic enzyme supplementation, and instructions for pain and constipation management. Follow-up was arranged with gastroenterology and primary care.
